title: ETRNL Agent Output Contract v1
doc: Lean, machine-checkable contract every etrnl agent emits at the end of its response. The validator (scripts/agent-output-contract.mjs) turns this from advisory prose into a hard gate: it parses the fenced block, checks the status enum, the per-finding line grammar, the deterministic status rule (status must MATCH the findings), two-tier verbosity for fenced-critical findings, and per-agent required fields. Not a JSON Schema for JSON payloads — a spec the validator reads.

status.doc: Two profiles. REVIEWER (default): status in reviewerStatuses; deterministic rule (enforced) — any finding with severity 'bug' -> blocked; else any finding -> changes_requested; else -> verified; a declared status that disagrees with the findings is a hard failure (anti-gaming). WORKER (scout/investigator/executor/consumer-tracer, which emit evidence/maps not verdicts): status in workerStatuses; any 'bug' finding still forces 'blocked', but 'completed' is valid with non-bug findings and 'blocked' is valid with zero findings (external blocker).

category.doc: fencedCritical categories carry the ponytail safety fence: a deletion/simplification lens must never recommend removing one of these guards, and a 'bug' finding in one of them REQUIRES the long source->consequence chain (two-tier verbosity).

findingGrammar.doc: One finding per line: '- <severity> | <category> | <file>:<line> | <problem> | <fix>'. Use line 0 for file-level. For a blocking (bug) finding in a fencedCritical category the <problem> field MUST contain the chain arrow '->' (source -> consequence), so an exploit path is shown, not asserted.

perAgentRequiredKeysDoc: Beyond the base requiredKeys, each named agent must also emit these fields. Reviewers not listed only need the base contract. ETRNL_STOP_CYCLE for the adversary must be <=3 (doubt-driven 3-cycle cap).
